title: Friday Quick Tip
subtitle: When a kid wants to quit
hook: A player tells you they want to quit.
intro: It is the middle of the season.
They say it quietly after practice.
statement: Wanting to quit usually means something else is wrong.
q1: Do you ask questions to find out what changed —
q2: or let the family handle it?
q3: What did they enjoy at the start of the season?
t1: There is no perfect answer here. But kids stay
t2: when someone listens to what is going on.
ctaLines: Ask what changed. Talk with the parent. Give it a week.
Talk it through or step back?
ctaPrompt: Share your approach below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
A player tells you they want to quit.
It is the middle of the season. They say it quietly after practice.
Wanting to quit usually means something else is wrong.
Talk it through or let the family decide. There is no single right way.
What do you do? Share your habit in the comments.
